fullPassage:
Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language.
(A) This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
(B) To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes.
(C) This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 적어도 일부 동물들은 언어가 없음에도 불구하고 생각할 수 있다고 가정해 보자. 이것이 반드시 그것들이 개념을 보유한다는 것을 의미하지는 않는데, 왜냐하면 일부 사고 형태는 비개념적일 수 있기 때문이다. 우리가 동물이 개념을 가졌다고 말할 수 있으려면 그녀가 생각할 수 있다는 것뿐만 아니라 특정한 능력도 보여줘야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① capable: be capable of + V-ing에서 형용사 capable은 올바른 어법
✅ ② lacking: despite + V-ing에서 동명사 lacking은 올바른 어법
❌ ③ showing → to show: 'we have to show'에서 have to 뒤에는 동사원형 show가 와야 함. showing(동명사)은 부적절
✅ ④ specific: 명사 abilities를 수식하는 형용사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: have to + 동사원형: to 부정사의 to와 구별하세요. have to는 '~해야 한다'는 의미의 조동사 표현입니다.

✅ ① nonconceptual: 개념 없이도 가능한 사고 형태를 설명하므로 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ capable: 동물이 생각할 수 있다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ specific: 특정한 능력이라는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ imagine: 상상할 수 있다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: imply(암시하다, 함축하다) ↔ prove(증명하다): 전자는 간접적 함의, 후자는 직접적 증명입니다.

questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front.
